nodes.label: "Why it's here" Note
nodes.rationale: The note is what makes agents' answers useful; it is the only field written for the developer.

nodes.label: get_project_stack Path Confinement
nodes.rationale: Reads only five manifest files inside the agent's folder, never via symlink, and refuses network/device/verbatim paths since probing \\host\share on Windows sends the user's credentials.

nodes.label: MCP Agent Access (narrow read, narrower write)
nodes.norm_label: mcp agent access (narrow read, narrower write)
nodes.rationale: stdio-only server, read tools open the DB read-only; update_resource is off until the user enables agent writes, because page titles could steer an agent into writing; untrusted text is stripped of invisible characters.

nodes.label: Network source allow-list (GitHub, HN, blogs, TIOBE/PYPL)
nodes.norm_label: network source allow-list (github, hn, blogs, tiobe/pypl)

nodes.label: Collection Link Images (collection-covers bucket)
nodes.rationale: Owner's app re-encodes preview images as 480x270 JPEGs and uploads them so viewers never contact others' link sites; known limit: orphaned folders if a modified client deletes rows directly.

nodes.label: End-to-End Encrypted Library Sync
nodes.rationale: Passphrase never stored or sent; Argon2id key, XChaCha20-Poly1305 seal with associated data binding account, generation and revision to prevent cross-account or replay; three-way merge with pre-sync backup.

nodes.label: Security Requirements for Future Features
nodes.rationale: Binding requirements: per-window minimal permissions, Rust-side IPC validation, app-data-only filesystem, AI consent and credential-store keys, authenticated local-only extension channel, frozen lockfiles.

nodes.label: Hardened Preview Fetching (SSRF Protection)
nodes.rationale: Every DNS answer and redirect must be a public address (private, CGNAT, NAT64, 6to4, mapped IPv4 etc. refused), capped redirects, timeouts and size so a page cannot make the app request the local network.

nodes.label: Native Dialogs from Rust Only
nodes.rationale: Backups and imports are chosen in dialogs opened by Rust so the webview never supplies a path; imports are treated as untrusted.

nodes.label: Discover (Repos, Star History, News, Languages)
nodes.rationale: GitHub has no Trending API, so Repos uses the official Search API for repositories created in the period, cached 15 minutes.

nodes.label: Tech Stack (Tauri 2, Rust, React 19, TypeScript 6)
nodes.rationale: TypeScript pinned to 6.0.x because typescript-eslint does not yet support TypeScript 7.

nodes.label: Fixed-Host GitHub API Client
nodes.rationale: Only fixed api.github.com paths, validated language filter and owner/name segments so input cannot add search qualifiers or reach another API path; token never returned to the UI.

nodes.label: Read-Only Browser Bookmarks
nodes.rationale: UI picks a browser from a fixed list and a validated profile id so it can never name a path; Firefox places.sqlite is copied because Firefox locks the original; removal only hides in library-memory.json.

nodes.label: Release Pipeline (ci.yml + release.yml)
nodes.rationale: Every push to main that passes CI publishes a signed release named v<version>-build.<run>, with notes generated from Conventional Commits.

nodes.label: No Secrets in Repository
nodes.rationale: The only CI secret is the release signing key held by the release environment; the Community key is Supabase's publishable key, public by design; the optional GitHub token lives in the OS credential store.

nodes.label: Signed Self-Update (minisign)
nodes.rationale: Package installs only if its minisign signature verifies against the built-in public key and the signed trusted comment names the exact file, so an older signed package cannot be re-served as newer; signing key usable only from main.

nodes.label: Least-Privilege Capabilities
nodes.rationale: Main webview gets only its own app commands, scoped opener for http(s), event listen and four frameless-window permissions; no fs, shell or http plugins.

nodes.label: Webview / Rust Privilege Boundary
nodes.rationale: The UI is untrusted-by-default web content in a webview; all privileged operations stay in Rust, and the security model is about keeping that boundary narrow.

nodes.label: Layered Architecture (domain / application / storage / thin commands)
nodes.norm_label: layered architecture (domain / application / storage / thin commands)
nodes.rationale: Domain has no infrastructure; application holds use cases and ports and depends only on domain; storage implements ports; Tauri commands are thin adapters that never hold business logic or call storage directly.

nodes.label: JSON-LD SoftwareApplication and FAQPage
nodes.rationale: SEO structured data mirroring the README FAQ.

nodes.label: Agent Setups Sharing
nodes.rationale: Only name, description and public source are kept; install commands are built by the app from ASCII-word names so a shared setup cannot carry shell text.

nodes.label: Community (Supabase, RLS, GitHub OAuth PKCE)
nodes.rationale: App holds only the publishable key; row level security and checked functions decide access; others' links are never fetched so opening a collection tells owners nothing.

nodes.label: Isolated In-App Site Viewer
nodes.rationale: Sites open in a separate native webview with no IPC access because the capability is bound to the main webview only.

nodes.label: Prototype Freezing (freeze-prototype.js)
nodes.rationale: Applied to the app UI only; Tauri's global freezePrototype is off because freezing breaks many websites shown in the viewer.

nodes.label: Strict Content Security Policy
nodes.rationale: Scripts only from the app bundle; style-src allows unsafe-inline because UI libraries inject runtime styles.
